research_question: Can a periodic dimensionless Gross-Pitaevskii equation split-step Fourier solver reproduce exact and convergent reference dynamics on independent NumPy FP64 and Intel Arc XPU FP32 implementations?
objective: Certify numerical checks and XPU screening only; archive downloaded external processed-observable data with provenance. No SST/Euler/PKLSA physical equivalence is asserted.
null_hypothesis: At least one preregistered numerical reference or convergence criterion fails; GPE solver numerical qualification is denied.
alternative_hypothesis: All completed CPU reference checks and the temporal convergence check satisfy their independently specified thresholds; optional Intel XPU screening also satisfies parity thresholds.
assumptions: Periodic grid on a dimensionless square of side L=2*pi
Conservative cubic Gross-Pitaevskii evolution with g>0 and no forcing or dissipation
Complex128 independent NumPy reference and complex64 actual Intel XPU screening
External Zenodo archive has processed observables only, not full time-dependent wavefunction fields
No physical dimension recovery without specifying length, time and wavefunction scales

equations.dimensional_check: All variables dimensionless after xSI/L0 and tSI/T0 normalization
Ratio of equal-dimension norms is dimensionless

observables.definition: Exact plane wave relative complex L2 error
Relative discrete particle norm drift and reverse propagation error
Minimum observed Strang splitting temporal order at fixed final time
Real Intel XPU versus NumPy FP64 relative field L2 error

steps.operation: Retrieve Zenodo public source and verify published MD5 and all ZIP member CRC
Propagate exact plane wave and reverse a nonuniform complex field using NumPy FP64
Split-step dt refinement at fixed final time with independent fine-step surrogate
Propagate same initial field using Intel XPU complex64 and compare to independent NumPy complex128

falsification_criteria.criterion: G2 fails if plane-wave error, norm drift or reverse error is >=1e-10
G3 fails if minimum temporal order <=1.75 or maximum surrogate error >=0.1
G6 fails if true Intel XPU relative L2 error >=7e-4 or GPU norm drift >=7e-4

edge_cases: GPU unavailable is a missing execution prerequisite, never CPU fallback
Complex FFT XPU unsupported kernel raises real execution error
Published processed observables do not constitute independent full-field confirmation
Source failure prevents source-integrity claim but should not suppress numerically independent diagnostics
predictions: Plane wave error at periodic commensurate wavenumbers is near rounding error
Strang split step is asymptotically second order for smooth periodic fields
GPU complex64 reference error stays below preset screening threshold on supported Intel Arc GPU
